title: Predict: lazy Initialisation Order
hints: Stored defaults run during init; `lazy` runs once on first access; computed runs every time.
`computing eager` prints before `created`; `computing lazy` prints once; `computing computed` prints on both reads.
jsBridge: `lazy var` evaluates its initialiser on first access, like a memoised JS getter. A computed property re-runs every time, and a closure-initialised stored property (`= { … }()`) runs once at init.

compass.q: How would you write a lazy memoised property in JS (getter + `Object.defineProperty`)? What does Swift's `lazy` do for you?
Is `lazy var` thread-safe? What happens when two threads touch it first at the same time?
`lazy var` vs computed `var` vs `let x = { … }()`: when does each closure run, and how many times?
`lazy var dateFormatter` is a classic. Why are formatters worth caching?
